description: `pipeline/sending-engine.js`, `sendTestEmail()`: missing SMTP credentials records a simulated `sent` event and returns `ok:true`.
acceptance: Return actionable disconnected error; zero send/delivery records. Test API and UI with empty, partial, invalid, and revoked credentials.
tests: UI browser check: partial SMTP credentials

evidence.note: Covers actual loopback SMTP handshake, empty/partial/invalid settings, and rejected auth. Browser check covers the Test SMTP UI with partial credentials. Live/revoked provider mailbox credentials remain unverified.

evidence.command: Playwright browser acceptance against isolated UI servers
evidence.result: 9 routes, 3 viewport widths, batch create and partial-credential SMTP UI passed; 0 page errors
evidence.note: Mutations used only the disposable port 3001 database.

Empty/partial/invalid SMTP settings fail closed; local loopback SMTP handshake and authentication rejection are exercised; API and UI responses were checked. This verifies local behavior only. External provider mailbox credentials remain a P22 live-validation item.

description: Same file, `processSendQueue()`: `Math.random()` supplies send success and simulated soft bounces when credentials are absent.
acceptance: Delete production simulation branch. Missing transport never becomes sent/delivered/bounced. Real provider errors have classified causes.

description: Real SMTP path inserts `delivered` immediately after Nodemailer returns.
acceptance: Record provider acceptance; delivery is separately verified from authentic delivery evidence, otherwise unknown. Test delayed DSN and no-DSN cases.

description: `checkDomainDns()`: `dkim_ok` inferred from SPF + DMARC presence.
acceptance: Discover/configure actual selector, check key and captured message signature/alignment; missing selector is unknown. SPF/DMARC presence is not authentication success.

description: Same DNS logic looks up a website/domain A record and treats every successful DNSBL response as a listing; errors imply not listed.
acceptance: Distinguish sender IP/domain lists, query permissions, error codes, unavailable checks and actual evidence. Do not call this mailbox blacklist proof.

description: `pipeline/personalizer.js`, `callBedrock()` simply returns null.
acceptance: Implement official provider SDK adapter or mark disabled; no claim that cloud polishing ran. Live test with configured credentials before declaring enabled support.

description: `factCheckDraft()` returns `passed:true` on Ollama failure.
acceptance: Store `unavailable` and block automatic approval/send; human review cannot falsely turn a missing check into AI-verified evidence.

description: `server.js` analytics estimates tokens/cost from copy counts (`*380`, `*0.003`) and a constant cost-per-reply numerator.
acceptance: Store actual request usage and dated rate-card provenance. Label unavoidable estimates; unknown usage remains null. No fabricated calls/tokens/spend.

description: `pipeline/crm-sync.js`: generic `upsertLead` mutation and local fallback return `synced:true`; HTTP 200 is accepted without inspecting GraphQL errors.
acceptance: Verify real pinned CRM schema, persist remote IDs, inspect response errors, maintain retry/conflict status. Failure/offline means not synchronized.

description: CLI imports `runPersonalizationBatch`, but module exports `personalizeBatch`.
acceptance: Fix import/call; prove the ESM CLI starts for every command. This static import can break the entire CLI before its switch executes.

description: CLI/package script mismatch: `import`, `seed`, `batch-status`, `template` are advertised without switch cases.
acceptance: Implement truthful supported commands; validation and nonzero exit codes; production seed prohibited. Test every package script.

description: UI qualification/verification cancel wrappers call non-batch `/cancel`; server only handles batch-scoped cancel. Batch-close wrapper also lacks a matching handler in the inspected server.
acceptance: Canonical API contracts and actual lifecycle endpoints; contract tests exercise UI calls against running handlers.

description: `js/api.js` replaces network/HTTP failure with empty/default success-shaped values.
acceptance: Explicit discriminated errors; UI distinguishes empty data, offline, unauthorized, partial, timeout, and successful zero counts.

description: `queueSends()` joins multiple personalizations and chooses their existing variant; it does not visibly consume `assignVariant()` or enforce campaign batch enrollment.
acceptance: Durable unique enrollment/step/variant assignment and campaign membership; one logical send per eligible enrollment/step.

description: Queue limits use already-sent counts, not atomic reservations; processor has no durable claim/recheck of pause, suppression, approval, or capacity at transmission.
acceptance: Atomic reservations/claims and a final serialized policy gate shared with stop/unsubscribe controls; concurrency/crash/race tests.

description: Queue writes ISO timestamps but compares with SQLite `datetime('now')`; pacing is reduced to a max 1.5-second sleep while config says 30–120 seconds; window settings are not enforced in that path.
acceptance: Canonical time types, timezone/DST-aware durable scheduler, real pacing/caps; tests for same-day due times and restarts.

description: `updateSend` writes `sent_at` for failed sends; runtime throws become `soft_bounce` regardless of cause.
acceptance: Separate attempted/accepted/sent/delivered/failed timestamps, auth/network/provider/DSN error taxonomy.

description: Compliance helper functions exist but the real send path sends a mailto unsubscribe header rather than using the HTTPS token/footer helpers.
acceptance: Apply verified current sender policy; tested MIME with real business identity/address and HTTPS one-click semantics.

description: Warm-up eligibility is inferred from elapsed days; calendar ramp is not evidence of actual warm-up activity or inbox placement.
acceptance: Separate scheduled volume ramp from measured warm-up/placement results. Require explicit policy and evidence; never synthesize received/opened/replied events.

description: `reply-tracker.js` stores message headers but attributes replies to latest send by address; interested reply changes status to `won`.
acceptance: Thread/mailbox/message references with fallback confidence; interested != opportunity won or meeting booked. Cancellation must not wait for AI.

evidence.result: 49/49 pass, exit 0; B20 focused tests 6/6 pass
evidence.note: In-Reply-To attribution honors receiving mailbox; ambiguous address fallback stays unattributed; duplicate Message-ID is idempotent; classifier failure remains unclassified; interested replies do not mark a sale won. Live mailbox/webhook integration remains unverified.

description: `archiver.js` declares terminal states but archives all batch leads; deletes related rows without full relationship/schema preservation.
acceptance: Eligible lifecycle guards, transactional complete preservation, restore/reconciliation and FK tests. Never archive active sequence recipients.

description: `database.js` catches migration errors silently; archive fields diverge; failed migration can leave partial schema.
acceptance: Versioned transactional migrations with explicit failure and rollback; test old snapshots and all columns/relationships.

description: Server has no visible authentication/tenant boundary; wildcard CORS; raw project directory static serving; no body-size cap.
acceptance: Auth/RBAC/tenant isolation, static asset allowlist, strict input limits and secure transport. DB/config/source/secret downloads must be denied.

description: Crawling protection differs across fetch, enrichment, screenshot and browser paths. A DNS check followed by ordinary fetch needs rebinding review.
acceptance: Central sandbox/egress policy including redirects, DNS/IP pinning where appropriate, IPv6, browser subresources and cloud metadata.

description: Raw data is interpolated into HTML templates; click handler redirects to arbitrary supplied URL; tracking has sequential IDs.
acceptance: Safe rendering/sanitization, opaque signed tracking identifiers and stored redirect targets, no open redirect or forged analytics.

description: Verification suspicious-name heuristic can reject an address before DNS/SMTP and populate unobserved MX/check fields.
acceptance: Pattern suspicion is a flag; SMTP/MX outputs require observed evidence. Provider refusal/timeouts remain unknown, not nonexistent.

evidence.note: Unusual digit-heavy, consonant-heavy, and repeated-character local parts pass syntax validation; malformed addresses still fail. External DNS/SMTP deliverability checks remain environment-dependent and unverified.

evidence.result: 43/43 pass, exit 0; B26 focused tests 3/3 pass
evidence.note: Reacher result remains risky when SMTP evidence is null; deliverable requires explicit SMTP acceptance; MX host comes only from the observed response. Live DNS/SMTP validation remains unverified.

description: Verifier cache refresh interval keeps completed CLI process alive
acceptance: All CLI commands exit after completion without force-exit

description: Dependency audit found high vulnerabilities in nodemailer, undici and cheerio dependency paths
acceptance: Dependency updates are pinned/reconciled and tests plus audit pass
